known_limitation: SEMANTIC COHERENCE IS THE LIMITING DEFECT, and it is a limitation of the METHOD, not a bug to be patched. Items are composed orthogonally from a frame, a population and an ethical feature, but those three are not semantically independent: a records-only study cannot enrol at a bedside, a job-training trial has no loan terms, a zebrafish study has no rabbits. Three successive keyword screens were added, each after READING samples rather than by prior design, and each caught a class the previous ones missed. After the third, a fresh 6-item sample still contained obvious contradictions. A mechanical audit flags 26 items (3.3%) across the four classes now detectable -- a LOWER BOUND, since general semantic incoherence is not regex-detectable and every class was found by reading, not by checking. Treat the true rate as materially higher and unknown. RECOMMENDATION: this pool is a scaffold for human authoring, not a norming-ready instrument. Norming incoherent items wastes the norming sample and, worse, injects noise that looks like genuine rater disagreement -- which the protocol's dip test would then exclude as 'contested', silently deleting real continuum coverage.
